title: Janapada of Kāśī
capsule: Kāśī was among the earliest and most powerful of the Iron Age northern Indian kingdoms, with its capital Vārāṇasī described in Pāli sources as twelve leagues in extent and 'the chief city' of all South Asia. Its rulers bore the dynastic epithet Brahmadatta across successive lineages, and the philosopher-king Ajātaśatru of Kāśī engaged in theological debates with Janaka of Videha; the 23rd Jain Tīrthaṅkara, Pārśvanātha, was born there to king Aśvasena (9th century BCE). Kāśī was finally conquered by Kosala under King Kaṃsa—'seizer of Vārāṇasī'—shortly before the Buddha's lifetime, and Vārāṇasī was later absorbed into Magadha when Ajātasattu annexed Kosala in the late 5th century BCE.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's general location in the Varanasi region is secure; its precise borders—bounded by the Sarpikā River to the north and the Son to the south—are textually asserted but archaeologically unverified.
